doc.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Clarinet in bebop and the swing revival
summary: Few clarinetists played bop; he keeps trying to swing and notes the revival.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well the clarinet didn’t transfer to that music as much.
Buddy DeFranco was about the only one.

Buddy is the only one, and then now Eddie Daniels, who is sensational. You know he’s just — it’s nice talking about him because he’s so fantastic. But I still like to try to swing the way Benny, Artie, both of them, had that pulse which very few people do nowadays. So I’m hoping as long as I last I’m going to try to swing.
Yeah. Well there’s a certain amount of swing revival going on right now.

Oh yeah. Yeah I hear Big Bad Voodoo Daddy. We had a little concert out here two years ago, and they were on the bill as one of the featured acts. I was on one side with all the swing stuff and they were in the, let’s call it the wave section, where they were playing all the more modern stuff.
